text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- A letter bomb which was intended for Interior Minister Caspar Einem's step-mother Lotte Ingrisch, exploded without causing harm. It probably should have arrived on December 3, the third anniversary of the first letter bomb explosion.
- At a meeting of senior Social Democrat party members future co-operation with Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party was ruled out.
- Sales ahead of Christmas are slow and turnover is expected to be down on last year.

- Austrians are very pessimistic about the country's economy as only 11 percent of the population expect an improvement, a study by research institute Market shows. Since the presentation of government austerity plans retail sales have declined.
- Austria is third in an OECD ranking concerning governmental expenditure for education, only topped by the U.S. and Switzerland.
- The Social Affairs Ministry has denied plans to force long-time unemployed into community service.
- Economic research institute Wifo says Austria will have to try and keep control of Austrian companies in the country, otherwise they fear a sell-out.

- Steelmaker VA Stahl said the downward economic trend in the steel industry to has slowed down and should improve in the near future. However, profits are still expected to be lower in the second half of the year.
- Listed Vienna airport wants to pay a higher dividend even though profits are lower.
- Social Democrats demand a maximum income level for parents receiving additional state benefits for their children.
- After Bank Austria and P.S.K., now Die Erste savings bank and Raiffeisen bank Vienna will lower their interest rates by 0.25 and 0.5 percent.
